messages:
Alex: Quick idea — can we add a small simulator control on the cost dashboard that lets SRE/product simulate routing policy changes and see estimated token + cache-savings delta in real time?
Maya: love the idea. do you mean a slider that changes % traffic to cheaper model variant and shows projected monthly $ impact? :chart_with_downwards_trend:
Alex: yeah. two knobs: routing split (canary %) and prefetch aggressiveness (how many tokens to prefetch for hot sessions). output is a sparkline + delta breakdown: model cost, cache credits consumed/saved, estimated tail latency risk.
Ben: main blocker is telemetry: we need per-invocation attribution that ties back to the route decision + cache fingerprint. currently we only sample 1/100 invocations for full econ fields.
Sophie: sampling kills accuracy for small routes. prefer a hybrid approach: always send condensed econ envelope with route_id + token_counts + cache_hit flag, then sample full payload for traces.
Sam: agreed. condensed envelope size < 200 bytes. we can ship that synchronously and keep heavy payload async. low overhead.
Alex: here's a proposed minimal schema for the envelope (for the api team):
```
{
  "ts":"<epoch>",
  "request_id":"<uuid>",
  "route_id":"string",
  "model_sku":"string",
  "tokens_in":"int",
  "tokens_out":"int",
  "cache_hit":"bool",
  "routing_decision":"{variant: 'A'|'B', reason: 'latency'|'cost'|'sticky'}",
  "latency_ms":"int"
}
```
Maya: minor nit — routing_decision as object will be annoying in protobufs. use routing_variant and routing_reason primitive fields instead.
Ben: also include quantization_profile or at least a model_version to map per-token cost. otherwise dashboard can't compute unit econ.
Sophie: UX question: where does the simulate control live? top-level per-tenant panel or per-route details? my vote: per-route details (so PMs can see impact on a single SLAs). global panel can have a multi-route composer.
Alex: per-route by default, global composer optional. the simulator should show a side-by-side: current vs simulated (tokens, cache credits, est cost delta, 95p latency).
Sam: for prefetch accounting we need to be explicit about who pays the prefetch token charge — route owner or shared cache pool. that affects chargeback UI.
Maya: we already debated shared pool vs charge-to-origin. for the simulator we can show both scenarios: "charge to origin" and "charge to pool" and labels with examples.
Ben: backend ask: need an endpoint to run simulations deterministically against recent workload sample. propose POST /api/internal/cost-simulate with body {route_id, split_pct, prefetch_k, charge_policy}. returns series of estimated daily deltas.
Alex: requirements: <1s response for small routes, run on sampled telemetry (last 7d), seeded deterministic RNG so PMs get reproducible results.
Sophie: add a UX affordance to pin a particular sample window (e.g., last 3 hours) so on-call can test hot periods.
telemetry-bot: Note: new condensed econ envelope schema approved by infra team for a 2-week pilot. Docs: https://internal.redwood/infradoc/econ-envelope
Maya: followups — Ben can you prototype the API and telemetry changes? I'll mock the UI components in Figma.
Ben: I'll spike the endpoint tomorrow. initial plan: store condensed envelopes in a high-throughput timeseries (partitioned by route_id) and run simulation as MapReduce over recent shards.
Alex: thanks. Sam can you write a short runbook for interpreting the simulator output (esp. prefetch charge implications)? we should avoid PMs confusing estimated savings with guaranteed billing changes.
Sam: on it. I'll draft and add examples showing how cache credits amortize across sessions.
Sophie: and we should add an explicit "uncertainty" band to the cost delta numbers (sampling margin).
Maya: +1. also we should surface a "preview rollout" button that will auto-generate a canary plan with expected cost impact and suggested canary % (based on traffic and latency headroom).
Ben: tough part: making suggested canary % safe across multi-tenant noisy neighbors. we'll start conservative.
Alex: okay team — next steps: Ben spike API + infra, Maya Figma for per-route simulator UI, Sam runbook, Sophie UX finalization. sync Friday 11am. :calendar: 
Maya: thanks — adding tasks in the dashboard epic now.
Ben: will post brief status in #eng-platform when prototype is up.
Sophie: thanks all.
